gloss: to get along well; to be on good terms

definitions.gloss: to get along well; to be on good terms
definitions.explanation: to maintain a friendly and harmonious relationship with someone

definitions.gloss: to make friends; to become friendly
definitions.explanation: to establish a good relationship with someone, often used as an instruction or wish

examples.japanese: ⟦{兄弟|きょうだい}→兄弟：00964_kyoudai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{仲良|なかよ}くし⟦なさい→なさる：01307_nasaru⟧。
⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{二人|ふたり}→二人：00622_futari⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧{仲良|なかよ}くして⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: Those two always get along well.

notes:
A common expression frequently heard in everyday life, especially among parents and teachers speaking to children. The imperative {仲良|なかよ}くし⟦なさい→なさる：01307_nasaru⟧ is one of the most typical things said to squabbling siblings.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {仲良|なかよ}くし⟦なさい→なさる：01307_nasaru⟧: get along (parental command)
- {仲良|なかよ}くして⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧: let's be friends
- {仲良|なかよ}くして⟦あげて→あげる：00546_ageru⟧: be nice to (someone)
- {仲良|なかよ}くして⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧: to be on good terms

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{仲良|なかよ}し→仲良し：11449_nakayoshi⟧: close friend, being on good terms — a noun or na-adjective, often used by or about children
- ⟦うまく→うまい：01279_umai⟧⟦やる→やる：02980_yaru⟧: to get along, to manage well — more casual and broader, not limited to relationships
- ⟦{付|つ}き{合|あ}う→付き合う：02291_tsukiau⟧: to associate with — broader meaning including dating

WRITING:
Also written {仲良|なかよ}くする or {仲|なか}よく⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧. The kanji ⟦{仲良|なかよ}く→仲良い：29434_nakayoi⟧ is standard.
